intro: Each post belongs to one of four angles and carries a short topic tag. The budget is how many posts each angle gets. Cadence: two posts a week, Tuesday and Thursday.

waitingOn.ask: Send a photo of you and Shawn for “17 years of making this place smaller.” You can upload it right under the post copy in Ordinal.
Approve the first three posts in Ordinal. They're scheduled and can't go out until you approve them.

angles.name: Playbook
angles.why: One every ten days or so, spread across the month.
angles.description: How you actually do the work, broken down so a reader could run it tomorrow.
angles.forYou: Exercises a brand team can run without you in the room: reading five claims out loud, designing every panel for the store that stacks it sideways, and what a first call tells you about fit.

angles.name: Proof
angles.why: Two case studies from your session with Shawn. More would come from another interview.
angles.description: Specific outcomes and the story behind them, with the numbers and the messy middle left in.
angles.forYou: Real Skidmore projects told from the brief forward: Little Ghost's bag as a billboard and Oh My Goof moving Goof Off from the garage to the kitchen.

angles.name: Stance
angles.why: Your strongest angle, one post in each of the first three full weeks.
angles.description: What you believe about where your industry is going, stated plainly enough to be disagreed with.
angles.forYou: Your core argument: different beats better, a package can break too many category cues, and "reach a younger audience" is a demographic, not a position.

angles.name: Human
angles.why: One personal post to open the month.
angles.description: The person behind the company: what you're learning, deciding, and getting wrong.
angles.forYou: Seventeen years at Skidmore spent narrowing the studio's focus, and why getting smaller is the plan.
